en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks opened their mouths before a morsel had been brought to them... [as above] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not open my mouth when a morsel has not been brought.
One must not open one's mouth when a morsel has not been brought."
Whoever, out of disrespect, opens the mouth when a morsel has not yet been brought to it, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it is unintentional … [and so forth] …
"Of one who is a first offender":
thus ends the first training rule.
